ranking.note: Raised from P4: the card describes removal of node internal types from index code, elimination of cs_main during sync and a startup race fix, and it is a stated prerequisite for #10102 and #15719 — that is core boundary work, not the minor definition deletion the solo reason cited; hence the large move up from position 15.
Raised from P3: it fixes misleading public API semantics before the C API stabilizes and is the stated prerequisite for #34374, so it cannot sit below it.
Moved down five places only because its prerequisite #34775 and the broader error/boundary and capability PRs come first; band unchanged.

Lowered to P4: by the card's own account it removes redundant accessors already covered by height lookups, unlocks no consumer and touches no validation — the category treats uncommissioned API polish as P3 or below.

inconsistencies: #29700 and #35646 attack the same problem — fatal/runtime errors conflated with validation state at the kernel boundary. #29700 is the broader design (util::Result/FlushResult through validation and blockstorage) and should be reviewed first; #35646 (removing M_ERROR via util::Expected) should be settled against it rather than in parallel, or the two will churn the same call sites.

Logging is split into two opposing designs. #33847 attaches logging to per-connection handles and context options and explicitly paves the way for multi-logger support in #30342; #34775 deletes those connection handles on the grounds that the backend is a singleton, and #34374 builds on that. A direction decision is needed before detailed review of any of the four; reviewing #33847/#30342 and #34775/#34374 independently will waste effort.

Order matters in the logging chain: #34775 first, then #34374 (struct-based entries, drops logging.cpp dependency). #30342 is stated to sit on a stack including #33847, so it cannot be reviewed ahead of that decision.
#29700 declares a dependency on #25665 (extended util::Result), which is outside this category; that base must land or be reviewed alongside it.

#32427 and #35187 both change substantive non-API behaviour as well as the kernel boundary — #32427 replaces the block index storage format (WAL, checksums, durability), #35187 alters the coin-fetching path in block validation. Both are kernel and validation and may warrant splitting the storage/validation core from the API surface.
#33117 is interfaces::Node/GUI/IPC plumbing rather than the libbitcoinkernel C API; it is in this category only on the margin, and its consumers are GUI PRs #870/#488, not external kernel embedders.
result.notes: The band spread reflects genuine differences: boundary correctness and new external capabilities (error propagation, concurrent block-index reads, UTXO-less validation, instance-scoped clock, node-type decoupling) in P2; logging plumbing and single-accessor additions in P3; one redundant-accessor removal in P4. No P1 was assigned — none of these is a regression or an in-flight failure whose persistence for another cycle would be seriously harmful; the strongest candidate, the logging design conflict, is a decision problem best flagged rather than banded up.
